messages:
Mira: kicking off thread for merlin-embed-lite-v2 onboarding. ran the standard holdout + short-query sweep this morning, pushing raw results to GDrive. TL;DR: fp16 close to baseline, int8 small drop, int4 noticeable regressions esp on short queries and small clusters.
Liam: link to results?
Mira: https://gdrive.internal/redwood/merlin_onboard/2026-03-01/results.csv (internal)
Raj: baseline model reference?
Mira: baseline = heron-embed-384-fp16 (our current production compact). experiments compare merlin-{fp16,int8,int4} vs baseline.
Sophia: numbers please — recall@1/5/10 and any cluster metrics you ran?
Mira: summary table: baseline recall@1=0.412, merlin-fp16=0.401 (-2.7%), merlin-int8=0.387 (-6.1%), merlin-int4=0.352 (-14.6%). recall@10 baseline=0.780, merlin-fp16=0.772, int8=0.768, int4=0.730.
Mira: clustering/structure: UMAP+HDBSCAN ARI: baseline=0.62, merlin-fp16=0.60, int8=0.55, int4=0.44. silhouette (avg): baseline=0.21, merlin-fp16=0.19, int8=0.15, int4=0.08.
Liam: ouch int4 drop is large. did you run per-channel quant or symmetric? config?
Mira: default run was symmetric per-tensor quant (our quick path). config used: `quant_mode: int4, per_channel: false, clip: 0.01`.
Raj: short-query breakdown? we saw those amplify errors before.
Mira: yes — short queries (<8 tokens): recall@1 delta (vs baseline) = fp16 -1.8%, int8 -9.0%, int4 -22.3%. medium queries (8-32) int4 drop smaller ~10%. long queries (>128) int4 affects less on recall but increases p95 latency.
Sophia: any failure modes or NaNs? logs?
Mira: saw rare norm underflow in int4 run when sequence len >512 -> `ZeroDivisionError` at normalization step. repro: `python eval.py --model merlin --quant int4 --max-len 1024` -> stack: `compute_norm -> eps=0.0 due to aggressive clipping`
Liam: is that clip=0.01 too aggressive? maybe we clipped zeroed out some scale factors.
Mira: likely. also saw cluster collapse where small semantic clusters merged with large hubs in int4 UMAP visually.
Raj: can we try per-channel int4 and a small eps bump? Sophia, you had that PR for per-channel quant heuristics recently?
Sophia: yes, I prototyped `quant.per_channel=true` + `quant.eps=1e-3` in the quantizer. quick config suggestion:
```yaml
quant:
  bits: 4
  mode: per_channel
  clip: 0.02
  eps: 1e-3
```
Sophia: per-channel should preserve small-dim scales and help short-query vectors. I'll spin the experiment.
Mira: queued per-channel int4 + eps=1e-3 run (exp id: e20260301-pc4). starting now.
perf-bot: nightly-embed-eval finished: merlin-fp16 latency p50=12ms p95=18ms, merlin-int8 p50=9ms p95=14ms, merlin-int4 p50=6ms p95=24ms (p95 regressed for int4).
Liam: p95 jump for int4 concerning. could be quantized kernels causing stragglers or extra emulation fallback.
Mira: saw higher variance on GPUs with compute capability <8.0 — int4 path uses fallback slower ops there.
Raj: any reranking attempts to recover short-query loss? e.g., shallow re-rank with dot+edit-distance or classifier on top?
Mira: tried lightweight reranker (logit-scale MLP on top of embeddings) — recovers ~40% of int4 short-query gap but adds 3–5ms. config snippet I used:
```python
# rerank pseudo
scores = dot(query_emb, corpus_emb)
rerank_score = 0.7 * scores + 0.3 * mlp_score(query_emb, candidate_emb)
```
Sophia: next steps I propose: (1) run per-channel int4 + eps (in queue), (2) try hybrid quant: int8 for projection layers + int4 for last layer, (3) run multilingual short-query subset tomorrow morning, (4) test rerank latency/quality tradeoff on 50k QPS trace. I'll open a tracking PR.
Mira: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/embeddings/pull/987 — includes repro scripts, plots, and the norm-fallback patch (adds eps guard).
Liam: can we also run a small ablation: int4 with higher clip (0.05) to see if clipping threshold helps cluster structure?
Mira: adding that ablation. queued ablation id e20260301-clip05.
perf-bot: experiment run e20260301-pc4 started on cluster slot gpool-7. estimated 2h.
Raj: great. thanks for the quick triage. keep notes on which slices (short, multilingual, code-like queries) break hardest — we'll need targeted regression tests.
Mira: yup — adding slice tests to the eval harness. will post updates in this thread when experiments finish. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: run e20260301-pc4 partial results ready (30%): recall@1 for short queries improved from 0.352 -> 0.378 with per-channel int4 + eps=1e-3. full run ETA ~1h.
